summary: ASTRA connects crew health monitoring devices with a web and server system designed for astronaut missions. Existing Uno and camera firmware can submit pulse measurements, sensor waveforms, temperature and humidity readings, and crew photos. The monitoring API validates and stores readings, supports safe retries and historical queries, and manages secure device sessions and private photo uploads. The web integration supports crew registration and ground-control workflows, including account deletion with monitoring-data and photo cleanup. This matters because reliable health records and environmental readings can help mission teams track crew wellbeing, while keeping data tied to the correct crew member and recoverable through device or network interruptions.
details:
ASTRA is a crew-focused health-monitoring system developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It connects onboard hardware to a web application where crew members can view their own readings, medics can monitor crew health, and ground control can manage onboard accounts and see a crew-wide overview.

An Arduino Uno and sensors provide pulse, cabin temperature, and relative humidity readings; paired camera hardware supplies photos linked to measurements. The Monitoring API validates and stores this data, while the web app presents current readings, 7- and 30-day histories, charts, measurement details, averages, and check-in countdowns. Colour-coded status indicators and contextual guidance help users notice unusual, missing, or stale data. They are prototype screening cues—not medical diagnoses. Cabin temperature is clearly distinguished from body temperature, and the system does not infer indicators that its sensors do not measure.

We used .NET 10, ASP.NET Core MVC and Razor Pages, C#, Entity Framework Core, SQLite, ASP.NET Core Identity, Bootstrap, JavaScript, CSS, SVG, Arduino firmware, and private Supabase photo storage. We considered privacy, role-based access, reliable data transfer, intermittent connectivity, and compatibility with existing hardware. Safe retries, secure sessions, private photo retrieval, and deletion cleanup help protect and preserve records.

ASTRA’s intended impact is to give crew and mission support teams a clearer, shared view of basic health and cabin-condition trends, helping them notice changes and follow up. Its creative contribution is combining simple onboard sensors with role-specific dashboards, visual trend exploration, and operational workflows in a single prototype—while being transparent about its limitations and the need for qualified medical judgment.
